hypothesis: Theorem AA-1 (paper papers/autocatalytic_artwork/paper.md) predicts, on a 6-step, 3-compiler world with specification alphabet |S|=4, experience alphabet |E|=4, and candidate compilers {K_a (diagonal 0.85/0.05), K_b (shifted 0.85/0.05), K_c (uniform 0.25)}, that the audience's expected one-step predictive log-likelihood (the analytical E_{s,e ~ P_S x K_a}[log K̄_μ_t(e|s)] averaged over 200 seeded runs) is monotone non-decreasing in t from t=0 through t=6, and that the mean posterior mass on the true compiler K_a at t=6 is at least 0.9. Theorem AA-2 predicts that the Bayesian update mu_{t+1}(theta) proportional to mu_t(theta) K_theta(e_t|s_t) is literally the Boltzmann compiler-ecology update of Theorem CT-2 with reward r_t(theta)=log K_theta(e_t|s_t) and beta=1, so a parallel Boltzmann-update trajectory agrees with the Bayesian trajectory on every (t, theta, seed) to numerical precision. Companion gate: at t=6 the Bayesian audience beats a frozen-uniform baseline by at least 0.1 nats.

controls.description: Every K_theta(. | s) sums to 1.0 across the |E|=4 experience alphabet; asserted in tests.
Every (s_t, e_t) sample uses a seeded Mulberry32 PRNG; recovery is exact under the seed sequence 1..N_RUNS.
The maximum absolute per-theta gap between the Bayesian and Boltzmann posteriors across all 200 runs and 7 belief snapshots (t=0..6) is at most 1e-12.
The true compiler K_a is one of the three candidates in the finite family Theta={a,b,c}, so the AA-1 well-specified-prior assumption holds by construction.
The per-posterior expected LL is computed analytically over the 16 (s,e) pairs, eliminating held-out sample variance and matching the theorem's E-notation.

gates.criterion: Mean over 200 seeded runs of the analytical expected predictive log-likelihood LL_t = E_{s,e ~ P_S x K_a}[log K̄_μ_t(e|s)] is non-decreasing in t from t=0 through t=N_STEPS=6, with 1e-6 tolerance for finite-run noise.
Mean over 200 runs of mu_6(K_a) is at least 0.9.
Maximum absolute per-theta gap between the Bayesian and Boltzmann-equivalent posteriors across all 200 runs and 7 belief snapshots is at most 1e-12.
At t=6, the mean Bayesian-audience expected LL exceeds the frozen uniform-baseline expected LL by at least 0.1 nats.
